dal: Rinse dry lentils; soak whole mung, urad or pigeon peas overnight if used. Chop vegetables finely.
Cover dry pulses with at least 3 times their volume of water and simmer or pressure-cook until completely tender. Stir in any cooked beans only after this step.

Heat the listed oil or ghee, bloom whole spices briefly, soften onion, garlic and ginger if listed, then cook tomatoes and other vegetables until tender. Combine with the pulses, add remaining ground spices and salt, and simmer 8 minutes. Add leafy greens for the final 5 minutes.
bean: The chickpeas, kidney beans, black beans and black-eyed peas listed here are already cooked, unsalted weights. Drain them. Chop vegetables.
Heat listed oil, soften aromatics, add ground spices and tomatoes, and cook 5 minutes. Add beans and remaining vegetables with enough water for a thick sauce.
Simmer 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender and beans are piping hot. Fold in herbs and any yogurt off the heat.
curry: Dice vegetables and protein into even pieces. Rinse leaves and chop aromatics.
Heat the listed oil, bloom spices briefly, soften onion, ginger and garlic, then add tomato if listed. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.

Add firm vegetables and protein with enough water to prevent sticking. Cover and simmer until cooked through; add soft greens, coconut milk or dairy toward the end. Finish with herbs and measured salt.
dryveg: Wash and cut vegetables into bite-size pieces; keep leaves separate from firmer vegetables.
Heat listed oil in a wide pan. Add whole spices, then onion or garlic if listed. Add firm vegetables and a splash of water, cover and cook until just tender.
Uncover, add greens, ground spices and salt, and stir-fry until excess water evaporates. Fold through coconut, nuts or lemon if listed.
rice: Rinse dry rice or grains. Dice vegetables. Soak brown rice or millet for 20 minutes if desired.
Heat listed fat and soften aromatics with spices. Add vegetables and rinsed grain. Add water following the grain packet directions; brown rice and barley need longer than white rice.
Cover and cook gently until the grain is tender and water absorbed. Add cooked beans, nuts and herbs if listed, then rest covered for 5 minutes. Mix yogurt off the heat.
khichdi: Rinse the dry grains and lentils together. Dice vegetables.
Heat listed fat and bloom cumin and other spices. Add grain, lentils and firm vegetables with about 4 times their volume of water.
Simmer or pressure-cook until both grain and lentils are soft, adding water as needed. Stir in greens and cook another 5 minutes. Finish with measured salt and herbs.
porridge: Chop fruit or vegetables finely. Use dry oats, semolina, flour or grain as listed.
For a savory porridge, soften vegetables and spices in listed oil first. Add cereal with water or listed milk, stirring continuously. Whole millet takes longer than oats; cook until tender.
For a sweet porridge, simmer cereal gently in milk or water until soft and fold in fruit, nuts and any listed sweetener. Divide into two portions.
pancake: If using whole lentils or grains, soak 4–6 hours, drain and blend with water to a thick batter. For flours, mix with enough water or yogurt to make a pourable batter.
Fold in grated vegetables, herbs, spices and measured salt. Rest 10 minutes.
Heat a nonstick pan. Use the listed oil across the batch, spread batter into small pancakes and cook both sides until set and golden. Do not eat uncooked batter.
fermented: Soak the listed rice and urad separately for 6 hours. Drain and grind with water to a smooth thick batter, then combine. Ferment covered until visibly risen, usually overnight; preparation time excludes soaking and fermentation.
Stir in measured salt and any chopped vegetables. For dosa or uttapam, spread batter on a hot pan with the listed oil and cook both sides as needed until the center is set.
For idli, grease molds using the listed oil and steam batter over simmering water for 12–15 minutes until a skewer emerges clean.
steam: Grate vegetables or blend soaked lentils if listed; combine with flour, yogurt, spices and enough water for a thick batter or soft dough. Rest for 15 minutes.
Shape into small dumplings or spread batter in a lightly oiled shallow steaming tray, using only the listed oil.
Steam over simmering water for 15–20 minutes until firm and fully cooked. Cool briefly before slicing. Finish with remaining herbs or seeds.
flatbread: Mix flour with measured salt and enough warm water for soft dough. Knead and rest covered 15 minutes. Cook any potato, cauliflower or other firm filling until tender, then mash and season.
Divide dough into 4 pieces. Roll thin; for a stuffed bread, enclose one quarter of the cooked filling and roll gently. Mix leafy herbs into the dough when listed.
Cook on a hot griddle on both sides until opaque and browned, dividing the listed oil or ghee across all breads. Serve 2 breads per portion.
stuffedveg: Cut vegetables to create a cavity or lengthwise slit; retain edible flesh for the filling.
Toast and grind nuts or seeds if listed. Combine with herbs, ground spices, cooked pulses or crumbled paneer, and the retained vegetable flesh. Fill vegetables.
Place in a covered pan with listed oil and a splash of water. Cook gently, turning carefully, until filling is hot and vegetable flesh tender; uncover briefly to reduce the sauce.
roast: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut vegetables and protein into even pieces. Mix listed oil, yogurt or lemon with spices to make a coating.
Coat ingredients, arrange in a single layer on a baking tray, and roast, turning midway, until vegetables are tender and protein is fully cooked.
Add fresh herbs or dairy accompaniments after cooking. Use a food thermometer for animal protein rather than relying on color.
scramble: Chop aromatics, tomatoes, vegetables and herbs. Crumble paneer or tofu; beat eggs if listed.
Heat listed oil, soften aromatics and firm vegetables, then add spices and tomatoes. Cook until excess moisture evaporates.
Add eggs, paneer or tofu and stir gently over medium heat until fully cooked and hot. Finish with greens and herbs.
salad: Wash produce thoroughly and chop. Cook any raw grain or lentils in water until tender, drain and cool promptly. Listed canned or cooked beans need only draining.
Whisk listed oil, lemon or vinegar and seasonings. Toss vegetables, fruit, cooked grains or beans, nuts and dressing together.
Serve promptly, or refrigerate in a covered container. Add crisp greens just before serving; log bread or other accompaniments separately.
raita: Wash and grate vegetables or dice fruit. Cook beetroot, pumpkin or other firm vegetables until tender and cool before using.
Whisk the listed yogurt with measured spices, herbs and salt. Fold in the prepared vegetables or fruit.
Keep chilled and serve as a side dish. If oil and mustard are listed, briefly bloom the mustard in hot oil, cool, and stir through.
chutney: Wash fresh herbs and produce. Lightly toast listed nuts, seeds or pulses; cooked chickpeas need no toasting.
Blend all ingredients with a small amount of water to desired consistency. For tomato, eggplant or other cooking vegetables, first cook until tender in the listed oil and cool.
Use as a condiment rather than a complete meal. Refrigerate leftovers promptly.
soup: Dice vegetables and aromatics; rinse dry grains or lentils if listed.
Soften aromatics in listed oil, add vegetables, lentils or grains and enough water to cover generously. Simmer until all ingredients are fully tender.
Blend if a smooth soup is desired, or leave chunky. Stir in milk, coconut milk or yogurt off the heat if listed, and finish with herbs and measured seasoning.
cutlet: Cook raw potato, grains or lentils in water until tender and drain thoroughly. Mash with cooked beans or crumbled paneer, grated vegetables, spices and herbs.
Shape mixture into 6 small patties, using listed flour or oats to bind. Chill briefly if too soft.
Brush with the listed oil and bake at 200°C, turning halfway, until firm and browned, about 20–25 minutes. These are baked home-style adaptations.
noodles: Cook pasta or noodles in unsalted boiling water according to the packet. Drain, reserving a little cooking water.
Heat listed oil and soften aromatics. Cook vegetables and any protein until done, add tomatoes or sauce ingredients, and simmer briefly.
Toss with pasta and a little cooking water to coat. Add herbs, cheese or yogurt off the heat when listed.
sandwich: Wash and slice vegetables. Cook egg or animal protein thoroughly if listed. Mash cooked pulses or avocado for a spread, or use listed cheese/yogurt.
Spread the filling on bread or pita and add remaining vegetables, herbs and seasonings. Use only listed butter or oil if toasting.
Toast or warm as desired. Divide into two portions; serve fresh.
bake: Heat oven to 190°C. Mix dry flour, oats and spices in a bowl. Combine listed milk, yogurt, egg, mashed fruit, oil and sweetener separately.
Fold wet and dry ingredients together without overmixing; add chopped fruit, vegetables or nuts. This is an unleavened home-style bake unless no flour is listed.
Spread in a small baking dish and bake until set and a skewer comes out clean, 25–35 minutes. Rest before cutting into two equal portions.
fruit: Wash fruit and cut into bite-size pieces; remove inedible skin, seeds and stones.
Combine with listed yogurt, nuts, seeds or herbs. If chia or oats are included, soak in the listed milk or yogurt for at least 20 minutes or overnight in the refrigerator.
Serve chilled as a snack or breakfast component. No added sweetener is implied unless listed.
drink: Wash and prepare fruit and herbs. Use pasteurized dairy; chill before blending.
Blend all listed ingredients with water or ice to the desired consistency. Do not strain out edible fiber.
Divide into two glasses and drink promptly; this is a beverage or snack component, not a meal replacement.
poha: Rinse flattened rice briefly, drain and let soften. Dice vegetables. For sabudana instead, soak until fully softened according to package directions and drain.
Heat listed oil, bloom whole spices, cook nuts and vegetables until tender, then fold in the soaked grain with spices and salt.
Cover and steam gently until fully heated; sabudana should turn translucent. Finish with herbs or lemon.
eggpoach: Dice tomatoes, onion and vegetables. Heat the listed oil in a wide covered pan.
Soften vegetables and spices, add a splash of water and simmer to a thick sauce. Make wells and crack eggs into them.
Cover and cook until whites and yolks are firm. Finish with herbs and divide between two portions.
stirfry: Slice vegetables thinly and cut protein into small equal pieces. Mix listed sauces and aromatics.
Heat listed oil in a large pan. Cook animal protein fully first if listed, then remove temporarily. Stir-fry firm vegetables, followed by softer ones.
Return protein or add tofu, add sauce and a splash of water, then toss until piping hot. Finish with seeds and herbs; rice is a separate accompaniment unless listed.
